question: What core toxicological principle states that virtually any substance can act as a poison if the quantity is large enough?
explanation: Toxicology teaches that safety and toxicity depend on the amount of exposure, meaning harmless substances can become dangerous in excessive quantities. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: What is the main difference between toxicokinetics and toxicodynamics?

options.A: Toxicokinetics tracks how the body handles a poison, while toxicodynamics tracks how the poison affects the body.
options.B: Toxicokinetics focuses on antidotes, while toxicodynamics focuses solely on initial absorption.
options.C: Toxicokinetics applies only to gases, while toxicodynamics applies only to swallowed liquids.
options.D: Toxicokinetics measures cellular receptor binding, while toxicodynamics measures kidney excretion rates.

explanation: Think of kinetics as what the body does to the poison (movement and ADME), and dynamics as what the poison does to the body (its impact on your tissues). You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: Which route of exposure is responsible for the highest number of accidental poisonings in young children?
explanation: Young children naturally explore their environment by placing objects and liquids into their mouths, making swallowing the leading exposure route. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: Why do inhaled toxic gases enter the bloodstream so quickly?

options.A: Inhaled toxins bypass the liver entirely and go straight to peripheral tissues.
options.B: The alveolar-capillary membrane is extremely thin and has a massive surface area.
options.C: Lungs actively pump foreign gases into red blood cells using ATP energy.
options.D: Gases immediately convert into water-soluble ions inside the upper airway.

explanation: The lungs are built for fast gas exchange! Their huge surface area and super-thin tissue barrier let gases diffuse right into the blood with almost no delay. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: What is a common cause of accidental poisoning among young children in many Nigerian households?

options.A: Commercial industrial solvents kept in clinical labs
options.B: Prescription antihypertensive tablets left on tables
options.C: Imported cosmetics applied to the skin
options.D: Kerosene stored in empty beverage bottles

explanation: Storing hazardous fuel in familiar soft drink containers easily misleads thirsty children, leading to accidental ingestion and severe aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: A farmer from a rural community is brought to the clinic after spraying crops without protective gear. He now has excessive saliva and muscle twitching. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: Lots of drool, sweating, and twitching after working on a farm are classic clues for organophosphate poisoning. These chemicals block an enzyme called acetylcholinesterase, causing the nervous system to go into overdrive! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: Why might a pulse oximeter reading look completely normal in someone with carbon monoxide poisoning?

options.A: Carbon monoxide stimulates the lungs to hyperventilate, boosting true oxygen.
options.B: Pulse oximeters often mistake carboxyhemoglobin for oxygenated hemoglobin.
options.C: Carbon monoxide physically increases the total amount of dissolved oxygen in plasma.
options.D: The device only measures heart rate and fails to detect blood gas saturation.

explanation: Standard pulse oximgs can't tell the difference between oxygen and carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin. It gives a falsely reassuring reading even when the patient is in danger—so always look at the clinical picture! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: How does cyanide primarily cause damage inside human cells?

options.A: It binds permanently to calcium channels in cardiac muscle tissue.
options.B: It directly dissolves the lipid bilayer of red blood cells.
options.C: It triggers widespread liquefactive necrosis in the esophagus.
options.D: It inhibits mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase, halting cellular respiration.

explanation: Cyanide attacks the powerhouses of our cells (the mitochondria). By blocking cytochrome c oxidase, cells can no longer use oxygen to make energy, leading to rapid collapse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: Which clinical findings form the classic triad of an opioid overdose?

options.A: CNS depression, pinpoint pupils, and respiratory depression
options.B: Dry skin, confusion, and elevated heart rate
options.D: Diarrhea, excessive sweating, and muscle twitching

explanation: Opioids depress the central nervous system and respiratory centers while typically causing miosis (pinpoint pupils). [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: A patient presents with dry skin, flushed face, large pupils, and a racing heart after taking an unknown drug. Which toxidrome is this?
explanation: Remember the fun medical rhyme for anticholinergic toxicity: 'blind as a bat, mad as a hatter, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone!' [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h5)

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing any acute poisoning patient in the emergency unit?

options.A: Securing the airway and ensuring adequate breathing
options.B: Collecting urine samples for toxicological screening
options.C: Inducing immediate vomiting to empty the stomach
options.D: Administering activated charcoal via nasogastric tube

explanation: Always fall back on your ABCDEs! Life support and stabilization always come way before diagnostic tests or trying to remove the poison. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h6)

question: Why is washing out the stomach (gastric lavage) rarely recommended nowadays for routine poisoning cases?

options.A: Lavage only works if the patient drank pure alcohol or petroleum products.
options.B: Activated charcoal completely replaces the need for any physical stomach cleaning.
options.C: The procedure carries significant risks of aspiration and mechanical injury to the esophagus.
options.D: Stomach contents empty into the small intestine within seconds of swallowing.

explanation: Passing a thick tube down into the stomach can easily cause bleeding, injury, or worse—pushing the poison into the lungs. That's why we rely on safer methods now! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h6)

question: Which drug is given as the specific antidote for a severe paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?
explanation: Acetylcysteine works like a rescue hero! It acts as a glutathione precursor, soaking up and detoxifying the harmful paracetamol breakdown product before it can ruin the liver. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h7)

question: How does naloxone successfully reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: It binds competitively to opioid receptors, displacing the narcotic drug.
options.B: It coats the gastric lining to prevent further absorption of pills.
options.C: It stimulates liver enzymes to break down heroin into inactive metabolites.
options.D: It directly paralyzes respiratory muscles to force a regular breathing rhythm.

explanation: Naloxone has a stronger attraction (affinity) for opioid receptors than the narcotic drug itself. It swoops in, kicks the opioid off the receptor, and wakes up the patient's breathing! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h7)

question: Why is keeping a strict check on hourly urine output so important in severe poisoning cases?

options.A: It measures the exact chemical concentration of the original poison.
options.B: It proves whether the patient drank water prior to arriving at the clinic.
options.C: It helps evaluate adequate renal perfusion and guides safe fluid resuscitation.
options.D: It prevents the need to check blood electrolyte levels.

explanation: Many poisons love to attack the kidneys. Tracking urine output is an easy, frontline way to make sure the kidneys are getting enough blood and fluids are working well. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h8)

question: A young adult is admitted after taking too many sleeping pills on purpose. They are now fully awake and stable. What is your most important immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins.
options.B: Initiate strict suicide precautions and ensure constant observation.
options.C: Scold the patient regarding the dangers of taking medication.
options.D: Restrict all family members from visiting to maintain hospital quiet.

explanation: Just because they look physically stable doesn't mean the emotional crisis is over. Safety first—keep them under close watch and arrange mental health support right away. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h8)

question: What is a key safety message nurses should share with families to stop accidental poisonings at home?

options.A: Keep all household cleaning products unlocked on the lower kitchen floor.
options.B: Always induce vomiting immediately if someone smells a strange chemical.
options.C: Mix leftover prescription antibiotics into drinking water to save space.
options.D: Never store dangerous chemicals or fuel in empty food or drink containers.

explanation: This is a classic life-saving tip! Putting fuel or chemicals in juice or soft drink bottles is a major trap for thirsty kids and adults alike. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h9)

question: Why is it dangerous to use traditional home remedies like forcing caustic liquids or oils down someone's throat after they swallow a poison?

options.A: Traditional remedies always cure toxic exposures faster than modern hospital drugs.
options.B: Community members refuse to visit hospitals unless accompanied by a nurse.
options.C: Practices like forcing caustic liquids or oils down the throat can worsen tissue injury and cause aspiration.
options.D: Myths prevent patients from paying their hospital bills on time.

explanation: Forcing things down can cause the chemical to burn the throat a second time on the way back up, or slip into the lungs and cause deadly pneumonia. Always educate gently against this! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h9)
